predictions.text: ICP sweet spot is 200-2,000 seats.
Buyer is usually a director of IT or head of infrastructure, not the CIO.
ICP runs today on a shared inbox and spreadsheets, not a competing ITSM tool.
Buying trigger is a compliance audit or a customer security questionnaire deadline.
Ticket backlog grows because nobody owns the queue full-time.
Can't report ticket volume/SLA compliance to leadership; it all lives in email threads.
New-hire onboarding takes days with no single system tracking access requests.
Employees DM the IT lead directly because they don't know where to submit a request.
On-call IT gets paged for password resets at midnight; no self-service reset.
Buyers worry a security review will take too long and stall the purchase.
Buyers assume the product is too lightweight to pass a SOC 2 vendor questionnaire.
Legal wants SSO and audit logging confirmed before signing.
IT directors worry switching systems implies they mismanaged the old one.
Zendesk: incumbent helpdesk, but no IT asset tracking.
ServiceNow is aspirational but unaffordable with a 6-month rollout at this size.
Jira Service Management occasionally comes up, mostly as a pricing comparison.
Position PerfStaq for mid-market IT teams underserved by legacy ITSM.
Not a ticketing tool: the operating system for IT service delivery for teams too small for ServiceNow.
Position as the modern, fast alternative for IT teams without a dedicated ServiceNow admin.
Lead with time-to-value, not a feature-parity fight with enterprise ITSM players.
Category is self-service ITSM for lean IT teams, not another help desk clone.
Win by being the system a 5-person IT team can run themselves, no consultants.
Acme was live in 6 days with zero implementation consultants.
Bramford cut ticket resolution time by 35% in the first month.
Contoso passed a SOC 2 vendor review using the audit log export in under a week.
Decision: stop saying 'ticketing system' everywhere, starting with the website.
Decision: every deck leads with time-to-value and the 6-day Acme number, not the feature grid.
Decision: pull the enterprise case studies from the mid-market deck.
